calls.head: Where the Oilers have the edge: the power play
calls.body: The Oilers are the league’s best for the power play, and the Ducks are around the middle. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one. Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays, and Anaheim’s power play has been near the bottom of the league for years.
calls.call: The Oilers’ power play creates more per 60 than the Ducks’.

calls.head: The Ducks’ edge in depth
calls.body: The Ducks are around the middle of the league for depth, and the Oilers are one of the worst. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.
calls.call: The Ducks spread their forward ice time deeper down the lineup than the Oilers.

surprises.head: Anaheim brought the hits
surprises.body: Anaheim’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 168, against their usual 105 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 30 games.

surprises.head: Anaheim couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Edmonton usually gives up some of the league’s most dangerous shots. Not tonight: Anaheim’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 4.4% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.3% (about 6.5% against Edmonton) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 25 games.

surprises.head: A rough night for Lukáš Dostál
surprises.body: Dostál allowed 5 goals on 17 shots, worth 2.2 expected goals: 2.8 more than expected. Starting goalies have a night this rough about once every 25 starts.

story.head: Bouchard sparks the Oilers back from two down
paras: The Ducks’ Nikita Klepov played his first NHL game. Jason Dickinson played his first game of the season, after missing the first three. Beckett Sennecke struck first for the Ducks on the power play early in the first. Sennecke scored his second of the night on the power play late in the first to make it 2-0. Evan Bouchard got the Oilers on the board early in the second. Kasperi Kapanen scored his 100th NHL goal on the power play later in the period to tie it 2-2. Bouchard, Vasily Podkolzin and Connor McDavid scored three goals in 4:56 late in the second to put the Oil up 5-2. Anaheim pulled Lukáš Dostál after five goals and turned to Ville Husso to start the third. Bouchard also had an assist. Leon Draisaitl finished with four assists.
Don’t let the score fool you: the chances were a lot closer than that. Devon Levi made 29 saves for the Oilers.
Connor Murphy took four penalties on his own. The Oilers improved to 3-0-1, and the Ducks dropped to 2-1-0.

items.text: Three straight wins for the Oilers.
Evan Bouchard extended his point streak against Anaheim to twelve games.
Cutter Gauthier’s five-game point streak against Edmonton ended.
The Ducks beat the Oilers in six games in last spring’s first round.
